Been a long-time Amtrak rider (family/friends/destinations along the East Coast). A few general rules of thumb:

  1. Try not to take trips that are more than 1 day. You said that it'd be around 14 hours driving, so see how long the train is.

  2. If you're doing a 1-day + trip, get a sleeper car. Trying to sleep at night in a regular seat can be somewhat miserable.

  3. If it is a 1-day+ trip, expect a stop in Chicago most likely. Or DC.

  4. For Amtrak, East Coast > rest. Trains have decent infrastructure on the East coast due to major cities being close enough together. Those 'scenic' trips across the heartland? Yeah, you're going to be staring out at nothing for hours (there's wifi/plugs on the train but don't expect great service).

  5. Expect delays. Very few routes (except high traffic ones like DC --> NY) run perfectly on time.

All in all, I would recommend Amtrak if you're either going somewhere on the East Coast or you don't mind the solitude/isolation/being delayed. It's a comfortable trip but not necessarily more so than driving.
